summary: PAPER-GHOSH-SARNAK-22 is a careful extraction of Ghosh–Sarnak's Markoff-surface paper: 63 items, 5 routes and 20 source issues. It was read against arXiv v3 (hash reproduced), with v1 and v2 compared. Its library items hold at the pins. A_HF(100,800) = 7,630 and the first Hasse failures reproduce, E15 and the review's corrected item 57 reproduce from exact counts, and the other source issues stand. There are 9 findings: 3 medium and 6 low. (1) Item 5 copies a false inequality from §1(d), h_M(k) ≤ h^±_M(k) for non-generic k. In fact h_M(k) ≥ h^±_M(k) + 1 for every exceptional k ≥ 5 (k = 5; 7,105 cases up to 100,800), and no source issue records it. (2) Routes 1–4, accepted 23 September, have reached none of the live blueprint issues (#1025, #1040, #1030, #1021). CA.4 was marked source_decomposed the next day without this paper, and route 5's Part II brief imports fundamental sets that CA.4 does not plan. This repeats this session's RT-PAPER-CHEN-24/5 and GMR-19/7. (3) RS-03, accepted after the review, narrowed CA.1 and moved Gauss sums to FF.1, so route 1's 'CA.1 supplies the Gauss sums' is stale. Low: (4) item 23 is 'planned' only over SL(2,ℝ) in BelyiMaps, while Chen-24/78 plans the ring version elsewhere. (5) E11's version history is wrong: v1 and v2 had (log K)^{−1/4}, which Loughran–Mitankin already corrected. (6) There is no sourceVersions field. (7) Items 3, 4 and 10 do not cite CA.4's Markoff nodes or GMR-19/1. (8) Two misprints in §10 are unrecorded, and Proposition 8.1(ii) is partly vacuous. (9) The report's counts are stale.

All 63 items against their v3 locators. Re-derived by hand: (3.1)(a) and (d), Δ at (−2,0,0), (−1,1,1), (2,1,1) and (2,a,a), Proposition 4.1's small components, Lemma 2.2's box U(k), the sector area C = ¼ log(3/2), the admissible density 7/12, Proposition 8.1's local conditions in cases (i)–(iii), and §9.1's completed sums (Σ_k A(k,p) = −1).

Numerical checks. Exact enumeration of F⁺ points and exceptional k up to 100,800: A_HF(100,800) = 7,630 (matches Table 4); the first positive failures are 46, 56, 86, 124; 342, 1,456, 16,432 and 33,624 are Hasse failures (E8 confirmed); 7,105 exceptional k ≥ 5 have F⁺_k(ℤ) = ∅. The negative side by hand: −2 = M(3,3,4) and −4 is a failure. Local densities by exact counts mod 3⁶, 7⁴ and 5⁴: δ₃(9) = 2/9, δ₃(18) = 4/9, δ₃(81) = 10/27, δ₇(49) = δ₇(98) = 34/49, δ₇(147) = 36/49, δ₅(25) = 46/25, so E15 and item 57's corrected formula are confirmed. findings.where: PAPER-GHOSH-SARNAK-22/5 (statement: 'h^±_M(k) = h_M(k) for generic k and h_M(k) ≤ h^±_M(k) otherwise'); sourceIssues (no entry); route 1 (ClassicalArithmeticCompletion CA.4)
findings.claim: Item 5 reproduces a false inequality from §1(d), and no source issue records it. For exceptional k the inequality runs the other way: h_M(k) ≥ h^±_M(k) + 1 for every exceptional k ≥ 5. (i) Small cases: F⁺_k(ℤ) is empty whenever k < 54, since the least value of u₁² + u₂² + u₃² + u₁u₂u₃ on 3 ≤ u₁ ≤ u₂ ≤ u₃ is 54. So h^+(5) = 0, while (0, 1, 2) ∈ V₅(ℤ) gives h_M(5) ≥ 1. The same holds for k = 8, 9, 10, 13, …, and for k = 1, 2 (h = 1 by Lemma 2.1's discussion). (ii) Large k: a count over k ≤ 100,800 finds 7,105 exceptional k ≥ 5 with F⁺_k(ℤ) = ∅, the last being 100,792. In every one of them V_k(ℤ) ≠ ∅ and h^± = 0. (iii) The general argument uses §4.1. Take k ≥ 5 and a negative node (−u₁, u₂, u₃) with u ∈ F⁺_k(ℤ). Each Vieta image of it has all coordinates of absolute value ≥ 3, and so does each Δ-increasing move from a positive node with coordinates ≥ 3 (x₂x₃ − x₁ ≥ 2x₃ ≥ 6). With all |x_j| ≥ 3 and k ≥ 5, every bracket 2(k − 5) + (x_i² − 4)(x_j² − 4) in (4.1) is positive. So each positive node of this upward tree has exactly one Δ-smaller neighbour, its parent. The upward tree is therefore closed under Γ: it is the whole orbit, and it contains no point with a coordinate in {0, ±1, ±2}. An exceptional k has such a point, and its orbit contains no F⁺-root. Hence h_M(k) ≥ h^+_M(k) + 1.
findings.evidence: arXiv v3 §1(d), p.5: 'Let h±_M(k) = |F±_k(Z)| where ± = sgn(k), this being defined for any k. Then Theorem 1.1 implies that for generic k, h±_M(k) = h_M(k) while otherwise h_M(k) ≤ h±_M(k).' The same sentence is in v1 (p.4) and v2 (p.5). §4.1, p.13: 'The expressions in the square brackets in all three formulae above are strictly positive when k is generic'; the bracket 2(k − 5) + (x₂² − 4)(x₃² − 4) is positive once |x₂|, |x₃| ≥ 3 and k ≥ 5, whatever k is. §8, p.22: 'the smallest value of the polynomial is 54'. Item 5 statement: 'h^±_M(k) = h_M(k) for generic k and h_M(k) ≤ h^±_M(k) otherwise.' The counts were computed exactly. Every F⁺ point with value ≤ 100,800 was enumerated, and the exceptional k were marked from u² + v², (u² + 3v²)/4 + 1 with u ≡ v (mod 2), and 4 + u². The same run gives A_HF(100,800) = 7,630, the value in Table 4, which confirms the enumeration.
findings.fix: Correct item 5 to: 'h^±_M(k) = h_M(k) for generic k; for exceptional k ≥ 5, h_M(k) ≥ h^±_M(k) + 1 (the F⁺-roots remain pairwise inequivalent, and each orbit through a point with a coordinate in {0, ±1, ±2} contains none of them)'. Add a source issue E21: kind error; affects nothing, since (1.6) and §7 count h^± and do not use the inequality; locator §1(d), p.5 (v3; also v1, v2); correction and reason as above; known new. The CA.4 blueprint should take the corrected inequality as a node with the regression cases k = 5, 58 and 100,792.

findings.claim: E11's version history is wrong. Theorem 1.2(i) is one of the statements that changed between versions. arXiv v1 (21 June 2017) and v2 (27 September 2017) state the lower bound √K(log K)^{−1/4}. v3 states √K(log K)^{−1/2}. A related point in the paper: Remark 1.3(a) says the Brauer–Manin-explained failures 'are of order of magnitude √K'. LM20's Theorem 1.4 gives ≍ B^{1/2}/(log B)^{1/2}, and CTWX Thm 5.8 gives a lower bound of the same order. The remark is off by a power of log K.

findings.where: PAPER-GHOSH-SARNAK-22/10 (status missing; 'V₀(ℤ) consists of the two Γ-orbits of (0,0,0) and (3,3,3)'); items /3 and /4 (notes cite only PAPER-MARTIN-25)
findings.claim: Items 3, 4 and 10 overlap mathematics that CA.4 now plans or that another accepted route sends to CA.4, and they cite neither. (a) Item 10's two-orbit statement for k = 0 is Markoff's theorem after rescaling. For a nonzero x ∈ V₀(ℤ), all x_j are divisible by 3, since mod 3 the sum x₁² + x₂² + x₃² can vanish only when every x_j ≡ 0. After double sign changes x is positive, and x/3 is a positive Markoff triple. CA.4/markoff-root-generation and CA.4/markoff-tree then give the orbit of (3, 3, 3). Only the Δ-statement (3.2) is new. (b) Items 3 and 4, the level sets V_k and the Vieta involutions at coefficient one, are the case n = 3, a = 1 of PAPER-GAMBURD-MAGEE-RONAN-19/1 ('x₁² + … + x_n² = a x₁x₂⋯x_n + k … The move m_j replaces x_j by the other root'). findings.where: sourceIssues (no entries); §10 p.34; §10 p.34 ('see Sec. 3'); Proposition 8.1(ii), p.23
findings.claim: Two misprints in v3 are not recorded, and one hypothesis is partly vacuous. (a) §10 says 'By the arguments in Sec. 7, we know that A_HF(K) → ∞ … A_HF(K) ≫_ε K^{1/2−ε}'. The Hasse failures are constructed in §8; §7 is the lattice-point count. The slip has survived each renumbering: v1 has 'Sec. 6', which was then the counting section. (b) §10: 'The number of admissible k's (see Sec. 3)'. Admissibility is defined in §1 and §4.1 and proved in Proposition 6.1; §3 is Bhargava cubes. (c) Proposition 8.1(ii) allows ν ≡ 0, ±3, ±4 (mod 9) but requires every prime factor of ν to be ≡ ±1 (mod 8). Then 3 ∤ ν, so only ν ≡ ±4 (mod 9) can occur. The other classes are vacuous, not wrong. The first case is ν = 23, since 23 ≡ −1 (mod 8) and 23 ≡ 5 ≡ −4 (mod 9), giving k = 1062. That k is a Hasse failure: the enumeration up to 100,800 finds it admissible, not exceptional, and with F⁺_k(ℤ) = ∅.
